# Decompose dashboard.dock.projection.LayoutAdapter into one class per concern

## Context

Operator directive (2026-08-31): `src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs` violates the one-class-per-file spirit — a single ~1200-line static class now carries multiple classes' worth of concerns, accreted across the dock family cycle.

## The Problem

One file/class owns at least: item projection + placeholder creation, header-action row assembly + the reserved-name guard, tab-chrome projection prep, rail/auto-hide collection, edge-band decoration, the whole-stack header overlay (symbol-keyed restoration), and overflow threading. Each is a separable concern with its own change cadence; reviews and diffs on any one concern drag the whole file.

## The Fix

Split into per-concern modules under `src/dashboard/dock/projection/` (e.g. ItemProjection, HeaderActions, RailCollection, StackHeader), each one class per file, LayoutAdapter retained as the thin composition point. Pure moves with unchanged public statics first; any signature change is its own justified step (a move PR must not redefine custody).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each extracted concern lives in its own file with one class; LayoutAdapter delegates.
- [ ] Public API (`project`, `collectAutoHiddenItems`, `decorateProjectedItem`, guard behavior) byte-compatible; existing unit/component suites green unmodified.
- [ ] No behavior change: the split is structural (verified by the untouched spec suites).

## Intake verdict — close as not planned

The decomposition goal is real; this ticket's implementation shape is not current authority.

The graduated [DockLayouts architecture discussion](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/17818) and epic #17836 already own this decision. Their **binding final package tree** keeps exactly three projection modules: `LayoutAdapter`, `Reconciler`, and `MotionSignal`; the epic explicitly says leaves may not add, omit, rename, or re-home a module without first amending that authority. It also carries the operator's greenfield hard cut: no compatibility facade or preservation layer.

This ticket prescribes the opposite on both axes:

- it adds `ItemProjection`, `HeaderActions`, `RailCollection`, and `StackHeader` outside the binding tree;
- it requires the current public statics to remain byte-compatible, preserving `LayoutAdapter` as the facade the hard cut forbids.

That makes this a parallel target architecture, not an implementation leaf, and executing it during the active resize/header-action stabilization wave would create conflict-heavy structural churn with no product behavior delivered.

If `LayoutAdapter` still mixes separable responsibilities after the current DockLayouts behavior wave closes, the correct next artifact is a **new** leaf derived from fresh source and Memory Core evidence, preceded by an explicit amendment to D#17818 / #17836's binding tree. Do not reopen this ticket.

Disposition: **NOT_PLANNED — authority-bypassing prescription and wrong sequencing**, not rejection of the broader maintainability goal.

— Emmy (GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra, Codex)
